title: Multi-Agent Yield Analysis For Circuit Design
problem: Semiconductor yield estimation is computationally expensive via Monte Carlo and existing methods (importance sampling, ML) lack consistency across different circuit topologies and sufficient practical validation, creating bottlenecks in manufacturing cost control.
motivation: Accurate yield prediction directly impacts production costs and market competitiveness; traditional simulation methods become prohibitive for complex modern circuits at advanced nodes.
method: YieldAgent uses a three-layer LLM-powered multi-agent architecture that analyzes circuit characteristics and historical data to dynamically optimize estimation strategies; incorporates Retrieval-Augmented Generation for domain knowledge and Tree-structured Parzen Estimators for hyperparameter optimization across different technology nodes.
key_novelty: LLM-powered multi-agent framework dynamically selecting and balancing yield estimation methods (Monte Carlo, importance sampling, ML) with RAG-driven domain knowledge and adaptive hyperparameter tuning.
contributions: Three-layer LLM agent architecture for topology-adaptive yield estimation
Retrieval-Augmented Generation integration for domain-specific knowledge
Tree-structured Parzen Estimator-based dynamic hyperparameter optimization
2.9× computational overhead reduction while maintaining or exceeding SOTA accuracy across 12nm and 40nm nodes
limitations: Paper does not discuss transferability to sub-5nm or 3D IC designs, nor failure modes of the LLM agent.
primary_theme: LLM-driven adaptive yield estimation framework for semiconductor manufacturing
